title: Micro‑Cockpit: Slot‑Level Throttle Matrix for Predictive Burst Scheduling
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Design a compact, operator‑focused control ribbon (Micro‑Cockpit) surfaced on Dedicated cluster pages that exposes slot-level throttle controls, predictive burst scheduling, and health signals without overwhelming on-call operators or squeezing out cost transparency.
acceptance_criteria: A compact control ribbon prototype exists for desktop and tablet breakpoints (Figma frames) and passes basic accessibility checks (contrast, keyboard focus).

Operators can: view per-slot health scores, adjust per-slot throttle multipliers, configure burst budget sliders, and enable/disable predictive throttle suggestions from the same ribbon without navigating to a separate modal.

Interactions include inline confirm/cancel for adjustments, a lightweight undo for the last change, and a visible small-moment toast that links to the rollout job when changes trigger a policy rollout.
Telemetry hooks are defined (event names and properties) for throttle changes, burst budget updates, and predictive-suggestion accept/decline actions so SRE can instrument regressions.
Design spec includes clear mapping to Console tokens (spacing, colors, icons) and a developer handoff sheet with component variants (compact, expanded, read-only).
design_notes: Goal: balance immediate operability with minimal cognitive load for on-call engineers during incidents. The ribbon should be discoverable but not dominant on the cluster detail page.
We explored three paradigms: 1) flyout inspector, 2) top-aligned ribbon, 3) inline badges with modal controls. Top ribbon chosen for low-nav cost and persistent visibility during incident triage.

Slot-level view: represents smallest allocatable unit (e.g., vGPU slot). Each slot card shows: health (sparkline + badge), current throttle multiplier, last applied policy (who, when), and predicted throughput impact if changed.

Predictive suggestions: lightweight blue suggestion chip appears when telemetry predicts upcoming surge. Accepting applies a non-blocking change with a short-lived canary window. Declining records telemetry.
Cost indicator: a micro cost delta is shown inline when operators hover on throttle controls (estimated $/hour delta using recent token throughput). Using the same underlying cost oracle as Optimize.
Accessibility: keyboard-first controls, ARIA labels for throttle sliders, and summary rows for screen readers. Contrast and colorblind-friendly palette used for health states.
Responsive: collapsed ribbon collapses to an affordance pill on narrow viewports; tapping opens an expanded sheet with identical controls.
Failure modes: if the predictive engine is unavailable, suggestions hide and a non-intrusive warning appears in the ribbon. If apply fails, a detailed error is surfaced with link to job logs.
decisions: Use top-aligned ribbon rather than flyout so controls remain visible while scanning logs and traces on the same page.
Expose per-slot throttle multipliers (float, 0.1-2.0) rather than absolute token rate; gives operators an intuitive 'speed' knob while leaving throughput math to backend.
Include inline cost delta instead of replacing with separate cost dashboard; small amounts reduce context switching during triage.
Keep predictive suggestions opt-in per-cluster to respect teams that prefer manual control; default turned on for trial clusters.
Implement optimistic UI for quick feedback with robust rollback paths via the undo affordance and explicit audit logs.
tradeoffs: Compactness vs. clarity: tightly packed ribbon reduces page real estate but risks misclicks; mitigated with slightly larger touch targets and confirmation for >20% changes.
Estimations accuracy vs. latency: cost deltas use a rolling-30m estimate to stay responsive but can differ from billing. We surface a tooltip to explain variance and link to cost dashboards.
Predictive automation: aggressive automation could reduce ops overhead but might hide cost impacts; we keep suggestions passive unless accepted by an operator.
usability_findings: Small moderated usability test (n=6 SREs) found operators preferred persistent ribbon over modal in high-noise tasks (faster median time-to-adjust by 22%).
Participants asked for immediate visible cost delta when increasing throttle — added inline micro-cost to address this feedback.
Some participants worried about accidental larger changes on touch devices — added a confirmation flow for >20% throttle changes and increased touch target size.
